events.name: Akihito enthroned as Emperor of Japan

events.enhanced_description: On November 13, 1990, the first known web page was written at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. This event marked a pivotal moment in the development of the World Wide Web, revolutionizing how information is shared and accessed.
events.name: First known web page written

events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 1990, Germany and Poland signed a treaty confirming the border at the Oder–Neisse line. This treaty was a significant step in post-Cold War relations between the two countries.
events.name: Germany and Poland border treaty

events.enhanced_description: On November 15, 1990, the Space Shuttle Atlantis was launched on a classified U.S. military mission, known as STS-38. This mission underscored the ongoing importance of space exploration and military applications of space technology.

image.caption: Space Shuttle Atlantis lifts off from Kennedy Space Center during the STS-38 mission.
image.date_qualification: Depicted date: November 15, 1990, as stated in the image metadata.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

locations.name: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

events.name: STS-38 Space Shuttle launch

events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 1990, Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev proposed a radical restructuring of the Soviet government, including the creation of a Federal Council composed of the heads of the 15 Soviet republics. This proposal aimed to decentralize power and address growing demands for autonomy.
events.name: Gorbachev proposes government restructuring

events.enhanced_description: On November 19, 1990, leaders from Canada, the United States, and 32 European states met in Paris to formally mark the end of the Cold War. This summit was a significant moment in international relations, symbolizing a new era of cooperation.
events.name: End of the Cold War summit in Paris

events.enhanced_description: On November 20, 1990, Andrei Chikatilo, one of the Soviet Union's most prolific serial killers, was arrested in Novocherkassk. His capture marked the beginning of a lengthy investigation into a series of gruesome murders that shocked the nation.
events.name: Arrest of Andrei Chikatilo

events.enhanced_description: The Charter of Paris for a New Europe was signed by 32 European countries and the United States, marking a significant step towards the end of the Cold War and the establishment of a new framework for cooperation in Europe.
events.name: The Charter of Paris for a New Europe is signed

events.enhanced_description: On November 22, 1990, British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher announced her decision not to contest the second ballot of the Conservative Party leadership election, effectively ending her tenure as Prime Minister after 11 years.
events.name: Margaret Thatcher announces she will not contest the second ballot of the leadership election for the Conservative Party

events.enhanced_description: In the first round of Poland's first presidential election since the fall of communism, Lech Wałęsa and Stanisław Tymiński emerged as the leading candidates, setting the stage for a historic political shift in the country.
events.name: Lech Wałęsa and Stanisław Tymiński win the first round of the first Polish presidential election

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 1990, Appenzell Innerrhoden became the last half-canton in Switzerland to grant women the right to vote, marking a significant milestone in the country's journey towards gender equality.
events.name: Women's suffrage is introduced in the last Swiss half-canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden

events.enhanced_description: On November 28, 1990, Lee Kuan Yew announced his resignation as Prime Minister of Singapore, passing the leadership to Goh Chok Tong, marking a significant transition in Singapore's political landscape.
events.name: Prime Minister of Singapore Lee Kuan Yew resigns and is replaced by Goh Chok Tong

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 1990, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 678, authorizing military intervention in Iraq if it did not withdraw its forces from Kuwait by January 15, 1991, escalating the Gulf War.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: UN Security Council passes Resolution 678

events.enhanced_description: In December 1990, workers from the United Kingdom and France met 40 meters beneath the English Channel seabed, completing the first land connection between Great Britain and mainland Europe in approximately 8,000 years.

locations.name: English Channel, United Kingdom and France

events.name: Channel Tunnel workers meet beneath the English Channel

events.enhanced_description: The German federal election held on December 2, 1990, marked the first election since the reunification of Germany. Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union won the election, allowing him to continue as Chancellor of a reunified Germany.
events.name: German federal election

events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 1990, a tragic runway collision occurred at Detroit Metropolitan Airport when Northwest Airlines Flight 1482 collided with Flight 299. The accident resulted in the deaths of 12 individuals, including 8 passengers and 4 crew members.

locations.name: Detroit Metropolitan Airport, Michigan, United States

events.name: 1990 Wayne County Airport runway collision

events.enhanced_description: On December 6, 1990, President Hussain Muhammad Ershad of Bangladesh resigned amid widespread protests against his regime. He was succeeded by Shahabuddin Ahmed, who took on the role of interim president during a transitional period.
events.name: Resignation of Hussain Muhammad Ershad

events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 1990, the National Assembly of Bulgaria elected Dimitar Iliev Popov as Prime Minister. This event was significant in the context of Bulgaria's transition from a communist regime to a parliamentary democracy.
events.name: Election of Dimitar Iliev Popov

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 1990, Slobodan Milošević was elected President of Serbia in the first round of elections, marking a pivotal moment for the Socialist Party of Serbia as it consolidated power during a time of political upheaval.
events.name: Election of Slobodan Milošević

events.enhanced_description: On December 11, 1990, following massive demonstrations, Ramiz Alia, the leader of the People's Socialist Republic of Albania, announced that free national elections would be held in the spring of 1991, marking a significant step towards the end of communist rule in Albania.

image.caption: Official portrait of Albanian politician Ramiz Alia.
image.date_qualification: Portrait dated 1985; it is contextual to the fall of communism in Albania, not a photograph of the event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Fall of communism in Albania

events.enhanced_description: On December 11, 1990, a catastrophic multi-vehicle collision known as the 1990 Interstate 75 fog disaster occurred, resulting in 12 fatalities and injuring 42 others. The disaster highlighted the dangers of driving in foggy conditions.
events.name: 1990 Interstate 75 fog disaster

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 1990, Jean-Bertrand Aristide was elected president of Haiti, marking the end of three decades of military rule. His election was a significant milestone in Haiti's democratic transition.
events.name: Election of Jean-Bertrand Aristide

events.enhanced_description: On December 20, 1990, Eduard Shevardnadze announced his resignation as the Soviet Minister of Foreign Affairs. His departure was indicative of the political turmoil and changes occurring within the Soviet Union during this period.
events.name: Resignation of Eduard Shevardnadze

events.enhanced_description: On December 22, 1990, Croatia adopted its first constitution, a crucial step in its journey towards independence from Yugoslavia. This constitution laid the groundwork for Croatia's future as a sovereign nation.
events.name: Adoption of the first constitution of Croatia

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 1990, a referendum in Slovenia resulted in 88.5% of voters supporting independence from Yugoslavia. This overwhelming support signified a pivotal moment in Slovenia's path towards becoming an independent state.
events.name: Slovenian independence referendum

events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 1990, Ramsewak Shankar was ousted as President of Suriname by a military coup. This event marked a significant shift in the political landscape of the country.
events.name: Military coup in Suriname

events.enhanced_description: On December 25, 1990, the Russian aircraft carrier Admiral Kuznetsov was commissioned into service. This event marked a significant addition to the Russian Navy's capabilities during a period of military restructuring.
events.name: Commissioning of Admiral Kuznetsov

events.enhanced_description: The Knowsley Heights fire in 1991 was a tragic incident in Merseyside, England, resulting in significant loss of life and raising concerns about fire safety regulations. The event prompted investigations into building safety standards and emergency response protocols.
events.name: Knowsley Heights fire

events.enhanced_description: The 1991 Darling River cyanobacterial bloom was the largest algal bloom on record, significantly impacting local ecosystems and water quality. This environmental crisis raised awareness about the effects of pollution and water management practices in Australia.
events.name: 1991 Darling River cyanobacterial bloom

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Czechoslovakia became the second Eastern European country to transition away from a command economy, following Poland's lead. This shift was part of a broader movement towards market-oriented reforms in the region after the fall of communism.
events.name: Czechoslovakia abandons its command economy

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, USAir Flight 1493 collided with a SkyWest Airlines Fairchild Metroliner at Los Angeles International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 34 people, marking one of the deadliest aviation accidents in U.S. history.

locations.name: Los Angeles International Airport, California, United States

events.name: Collision of USAir Flight 1493 and SkyWest Airlines Fairchild Metroliner

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 2015, a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Hindu Kush region, causing widespread devastation and resulting in 398 fatalities, with the majority occurring in Pakistan and Afghanistan. The earthquake's impact was felt across a vast area, leading to significant humanitarian challenges in the affected regions.
events.name: Hindu Kush earthquake

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, Jean-Bertrand Aristide was sworn in as Haiti's first democratically elected president, marking a significant moment in the country's political history, although he would be ousted later that year.
events.name: Swearing-in of Haiti's first democratically elected president

events.enhanced_description: The Provisional Irish Republican Army launched a mortar attack on 10 Downing Street during a cabinet meeting on January 1, 1991, demonstrating the ongoing conflict in Northern Ireland and the threat posed to British leadership.

locations.name: 10 Downing Street, London, England, United Kingdom

events.name: Mortar attack on 10 Downing Street

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, coalition ground troops crossed the Saudi Arabian border into Kuwait, marking the beginning of the ground phase of the Gulf War aimed at liberating Kuwait from Iraqi occupation.
events.name: Gulf War: Ground troops enter Kuwait

events.enhanced_description: In the Bangladeshi general election held on January 1, 1991, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party won 139 of 300 seats in the Jatiyo Sangshad, leading to Khaleda Zia's presidency on March 19.
events.name: Bangladeshi general election

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, a video surfaced showing the brutal beating of motorist Rodney King by Los Angeles police officers, which sparked widespread outrage and protests. This incident became a pivotal moment in the discussion of police brutality and racial discrimination in the United States.
events.name: Rodney King beating incident

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the U.S. and Canada signed the Acid Rain Treaty, a landmark agreement aimed at reducing sulfur dioxide emissions that cause acid rain. This treaty marked a significant step in cross-border environmental cooperation.
events.name: Acid Rain Treaty signed

events.enhanced_description: After seven months of exile in Saudi Arabia due to the Gulf War, Emir Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah returned to Kuwait City in 1991. His return symbolized the restoration of the Kuwaiti government following the liberation of the country from Iraqi occupation.
events.name: Emir of Kuwait returns after Gulf War

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, after 16 years of wrongful imprisonment, the Birmingham Six were released when a court found that police had fabricated evidence against them. This case became a significant example of miscarriages of justice in the UK.
events.name: Birmingham Six released

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the United States and Albania resumed diplomatic relations for the first time since 1939, reflecting the changing political landscape in Eastern Europe following the fall of communism. This re-establishment of ties was significant for both nations.
events.name: U.S. and Albania resume diplomatic relations

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, a national referendum in the Soviet Union saw 77% of voters favor keeping the 15 Soviet republics together, although six republics effectively boycotted the vote. This event highlighted the growing tensions within the union as it approached dissolution.
events.name: Soviet Union referendum on union

events.enhanced_description: In early 2023, Finland held a parliamentary election where the centre-right National Coalition led by Petteri Orpo received the most votes. This election reflects the shifting political landscape in Finland and the growing influence of conservative parties.

image.caption: Map of Finnish parliamentary election results by province in 1991.
image.date_qualification: The image was created on 2017-02-14; the depicted results are from the 1991 election.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Finnish parliamentary election

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, and Paraguay signed the Treaty of Asunción, establishing Mercosur, a regional trade bloc aimed at promoting free trade and economic integration among its member states.
events.name: Treaty of Asunción signed

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Georgia voted for independence from the Soviet Union, leading to the Supreme Council declaring the independent Republic of Georgia on April 9. This marked a significant moment in the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
events.name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Georgia votes for independence

events.enhanced_description: A significant solar flare in 1991 resulted in an unusually large aurora, visible as far south as Pennsylvania. This natural phenomenon captivated observers and highlighted the effects of solar activity on Earth's atmosphere.
events.name: Large solar flare triggers aurora

events.enhanced_description: The South African Parliament voted to repeal laws that prohibited Black ownership of land, marking a significant step towards dismantling the apartheid system. This legislative change was part of a broader movement towards racial equality in the country.
events.name: End of Apartheid: Repeal of land ownership laws in South Africa

events.enhanced_description: During the Sri Lankan civil war, Sri Lankan Army soldiers killed 152 civilians in Kokkadichcholai, an event that highlighted the brutal nature of the conflict and the impact on civilian populations.
events.name: Sri Lankan civil war: Kokkadichcholai massacre

events.enhanced_description: The Party of Labour of Albania was dissolved and succeeded by the Socialist Party of Albania, marking the end of communist rule in the country. This transition was part of a broader shift towards democracy in Eastern Europe.
events.name: Dissolution of the Party of Labour of Albania

events.enhanced_description: The Indian general elections concluded with the Indian National Congress winning the most seats but failing to secure a majority. This led to P. V. Narasimha Rao becoming Prime Minister, navigating a complex political landscape.
events.name: Indian general elections

events.enhanced_description: The South African parliament repealed the Population Registration Act, which mandated racial classification at birth, a significant step towards dismantling apartheid and promoting racial equality in South Africa.
events.name: End of Apartheid: Repeal of the Population Registration Act

events.enhanced_description: President Turgut Özal appointed Mesut Yılmaz as Prime Minister of Turkey following the resignation of Yıldırım Akbulut. Yılmaz's government was formed on June 23, 1991, and lasted until November of the same year.
events.name: Appointment of Mesut Yılmaz as Prime Minister of Turkey

events.enhanced_description: Harry Collinson, a planning officer for Derwentside District Council, was shot dead at Butsfield, County Durham, in an incident that was captured on camera by a BBC regional news crew, drawing significant media attention.
events.name: Harry Collinson murder

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the Warsaw Pact was officially dissolved in Prague, marking the end of a military alliance that had existed since 1955. This event symbolized the waning influence of the Soviet Union in Eastern Europe and the shift towards democratic governance in the region.
events.name: Dissolution of the Warsaw Pact

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the world's first GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) telephone call was made in Finland, representing a significant advancement in mobile telecommunications technology. This innovation laid the groundwork for the modern mobile phone industry and global connectivity.
events.name: First GSM Telephone Call

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Alan Fiers, a key figure in the Iran–Contra affair, agreed to plead guilty to two charges of lying to the U.S. Congress. This scandal involved secret U.S. arms sales to Iran and the diversion of funds to Contra rebels in Nicaragua, raising serious questions about government accountability.
events.name: Iran–Contra Affair: Alan Fiers Pleads Guilty

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, Nigeria Airways Flight 2120, a Douglas DC-8 operated by Canadian airline Nolisair, caught fire and crashed shortly after takeoff from Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, resulting in the tragic loss of all 261 people on board. This incident raised concerns about aviation safety and emergency response protocols.
events.name: Nigeria Airways Flight 2120 Crash

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Linus Torvalds posted a message to the Usenet newsgroup comp.os.minix, announcing the development of a new operating system kernel named Linux. This event marked the beginning of a significant movement in open-source software development.
events.name: Linus Torvalds posts messages to the Usenet newsgroup comp

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, Michael Schumacher made his debut in Formula One racing at the Belgian Grand Prix, marking the start of a legendary career that would see him become one of the most successful drivers in the sport's history.
events.name: Michael Schumacher makes his Formula One debut at the Belgian Grand Prix

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, during the Iraq disarmament crisis, the UN Security Council passed Resolution 715, demanding that Iraq accept unconditionally the inspectors designated by the Special Commission. Iraq rejected the resolution, calling it unlawful, escalating tensions in the region.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: UN Security Council passes Resolution 715

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the leaders of the Baltic States—Arnold Rüütel of Estonia, Anatolijs Gorbunovs of Latvia, and Vytautas Landsbergis of Lithuania—signed the OSCE Final Act in Helsinki, Finland. This agreement was significant for the Baltic nations as they sought greater independence and recognition on the international stage.
events.name: Leaders of Baltic States sign OSCE Final Act

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the Oh-My-God particle, the highest energy cosmic ray ever recorded, was detected. This discovery provided significant insights into cosmic rays and their origins, contributing to the field of astrophysics.
events.name: Oh-My-God particle detected

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, a large suburban firestorm centered in Oakland Hills, California, resulted in the deaths of 25 people and injuries to 150 others. This devastating fire highlighted the risks of wildfires in urban areas.
events.name: Oakland Hills firestorm

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, a 6.8 Mw earthquake struck Uttarkashi, India, killing at least 768 people and destroying thousands of homes. This disaster underscored the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.

image.caption: USGS ShakeMap for the Uttarkashi earthquake.
image.credit: United States Geological Survey — first version: [1] , second version: [2]
image.date_qualification: A USGS ShakeMap depicting the earthquake; image date is 2016-11-11, not the date of the 1991 event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Uttarkashi earthquake

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, China and Vietnam restored diplomatic relations after a 13-year rift that followed the 1979 Sino-Vietnamese War. This restoration marked a significant step towards normalizing relations between the two countries and fostering regional stability.
events.name: China and Vietnam restore diplomatic relations

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Cambodian Prince Norodom Sihanouk returned to Phnom Penh after 13 years of exile. His return was a pivotal moment in Cambodia's political landscape, signaling a potential end to years of conflict and instability.
events.name: Cambodian Prince Norodom Sihanouk returns to Phnom Penh

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, during the Lebanon Hostage Crisis, Anglican Church envoys Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland were set free by their kidnappers in Beirut. Their release marked a significant moment in the ongoing crisis that had seen numerous foreign nationals taken hostage.
events.name: Lebanon Hostage Crisis: Release of Anglican Church envoys

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1991, journalist Terry A. Anderson was released after seven years of captivity during the Lebanon Hostage Crisis, marking the end of the longest-held American hostage situation in Lebanon.
events.name: Lebanon Hostage Crisis: Journalist Terry A. Anderson is released

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, John Leonard Orr, one of the most notorious serial arsonists of the 20th century, was arrested in Los Angeles, California, after a lengthy investigation into a series of devastating fires.
events.name: John Leonard Orr is arrested in California

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the Nigerian government officially moved its capital from Lagos to Abuja, a decision aimed at promoting national unity and reducing congestion in Lagos.
events.name: Nigeria moves its capital from Lagos to Abuja

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, Ukraine became the first post-Soviet republic to decriminalize homosexuality, reflecting a significant shift in social attitudes and legal reforms following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
events.name: Ukraine decriminalizes homosexuality

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the Skarnsund Bridge was inaugurated in Norway, becoming the world's longest cable-stayed bridge for two years, with a remarkable span of 530 meters (1,739 feet).

image.caption: View west along the Skarnsund Bridge carriageway in Norway.
image.date_qualification: A view of the bridge, not a photograph of its 1991 opening. The image date is not provided; the 2008 timestamp is an upload or metadata date, not a supported depicted date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Skarnsund Bridge opens in Norway

events.enhanced_description: In 1991, the Russian SFSR officially renamed itself the Russian Federation, signifying a new political identity following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
events.name: The Russian SFSR renames itself the Russian Federation

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 1991, Georgian troops launched an attack on Tskhinvali, the capital of South Ossetia, igniting the 1991–92 South Ossetia War. This conflict arose amid rising tensions over the status of South Ossetia and was part of the broader disintegration of the Soviet Union.
events.name: Georgian troops attack Tskhinvali, starting the South Ossetia War

events.enhanced_description: On January 7, 1991, an attempted coup by the Tonton Macoute, a paramilitary group loyal to former dictator Jean-Claude Duvalier, was thwarted in Haiti. This event was part of the political turmoil following the election of Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide.
events.name: 1991 Haitian coup d'état thwarted

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 1991, U.S. Secretary of State James Baker met with Iraqi Foreign Minister Tariq Aziz in an attempt to negotiate a withdrawal of Iraqi troops from Kuwait. The talks ultimately failed, escalating tensions that would lead to military action.
events.name: U.S. Secretary of State James Baker meets with Iraqi Foreign Minister Tariq Aziz

events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 1991, the 102nd U.S. Congress passed a resolution authorizing the use of military force to expel Iraqi forces from Kuwait. This decision was a pivotal moment in the Gulf War, setting the stage for Operation Desert Storm.
events.name: U.S. Congress authorizes military force in Gulf War

events.enhanced_description: On January 13, 1991, Soviet forces stormed Vilnius in an attempt to suppress the Lithuanian independence movement, resulting in the deaths of 14 civilians and injuring over 700. This brutal crackdown was part of the broader struggle for independence in the Baltic states.
events.name: Soviet forces storm Vilnius during the Singing Revolution

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 1991, the United Nations deadline for the withdrawal of Iraqi forces from Kuwait expired. This expiration set the stage for the commencement of Operation Desert Storm, marking a significant escalation in the Gulf War.

image.caption: Israeli civilians take shelter from missiles during the Gulf War.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States
