events.name: Vicente Fox Elected President of Mexico

events.enhanced_description: A series of suicide bombings in Chechnya in July 2000 marked a significant escalation in the conflict between Chechen separatists and Russian forces. These attacks resulted in numerous casualties and highlighted the ongoing instability in the region.
events.name: July 2000 Chechnya suicide bombings

events.enhanced_description: On July 7, 2000, the draft assembly of the Human Genome Project was announced at the White House by President Bill Clinton, along with scientists Francis Collins and Craig Venter. This announcement represented a monumental step in understanding human genetics and its implications for medicine.
events.name: Human Genome Project Draft Assembly Announcement

events.enhanced_description: On July 10, 2000, a leaking petroleum pipeline exploded in southern Nigeria, resulting in the tragic deaths of approximately 250 villagers who were scavenging gasoline. This disaster highlighted the dangers associated with oil extraction and the need for improved safety measures.
events.name: Nigeria Pipeline Explosion

events.enhanced_description: On July 11, 2000, a summit meeting took place at Camp David between U.S. President Bill Clinton, Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak, and Palestinian Authority Chairman Yasser Arafat. The meeting aimed to resolve ongoing conflicts but ultimately ended without an agreement.
events.name: Camp David Summit

events.enhanced_description: On July 14, 2000, a powerful solar flare, later named the Bastille Day event, caused a geomagnetic storm on Earth. This event disrupted communications and power systems, showcasing the impact of solar activity on modern technology.
events.name: Bastille Day Solar Flare

events.enhanced_description: On July 25, 2000, Air France Flight 4590, a Concorde aircraft, tragically crashed into a hotel in Gonesse, France, shortly after takeoff, resulting in the deaths of all 109 people on board and 4 individuals in the hotel. This incident raised serious concerns about the safety of supersonic travel.
events.name: Air France Flight 4590 Crash

events.enhanced_description: On August 8, 2000, the Confederate submarine H.L. Hunley was raised to the surface after lying on the ocean floor for 136 years. This historic recovery provided valuable insights into Civil War naval technology and the submarine's role in warfare.
events.name: Raising of the H.L. Hunley

events.enhanced_description: On August 12, 2000, the Russian submarine Kursk sank in the Barents Sea during one of the largest naval exercises since the dissolution of the Soviet Union, resulting in the tragic deaths of all 118 crew members on board. This incident raised questions about the safety of Russian naval operations.
events.name: Kursk Submarine Sinking

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 2000, Tsar Nicholas II and his family were canonized by the synod of the Russian Orthodox Church, recognizing their martyrdom and significance in Russian history. This event marked a pivotal moment in the reconciliation of the Russian Orthodox Church with its past.
events.name: Canonization of Tsar Nicholas II

events.enhanced_description: On September 1, 2000, the Nokia 3310 mobile phone was released, quickly becoming one of the most popular mobile devices of its time. Known for its durability and long battery life, the Nokia 3310 became a cultural icon in the early 2000s.
events.name: Release of Nokia 3310

events.enhanced_description: On September 6, 2000, Bofors, the last wholly Swedish-owned arms manufacturer, was sold to the American arms manufacturer United Defense. This marked a significant shift in the Swedish defense industry, reflecting broader trends of globalization and consolidation in the arms sector.
events.name: Sale of Bofors to United Defense

events.enhanced_description: On September 6, 2000, world leaders gathered at the United Nations Headquarters in New York City for the Millennium Summit. This historic meeting aimed to address global challenges and set the agenda for international cooperation in the new millennium.

locations.historical_name: Bacchanal: A Faun Teased by Children
locations.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art

events.name: Millennium Summit

events.enhanced_description: On September 7, 2000, fuel protests erupted across the United Kingdom, leading to the blockade of refineries and halting the supply to petrol stations. The protests were driven by rising fuel prices and had significant impacts on transportation and daily life.
events.name: UK Fuel Protests

events.enhanced_description: On September 13, 2000, Steve Jobs introduced the Mac OS X Public Beta, marking a significant step in Apple's transition to a new operating system. Priced at $29.95, this beta version laid the groundwork for future developments in Apple's software ecosystem.
events.name: Introduction of Mac OS X Public Beta

events.enhanced_description: On September 14, 2000, Microsoft released Windows Me (Millennium Edition), aimed at home users. Despite high expectations, the operating system faced criticism for its stability and performance issues.
events.name: Release of Windows Me

events.enhanced_description: On October 1, 2000, the 2000 Summer Olympics officially commenced in Sydney, Australia, marking the first Olympic Games of the new millennium. The event showcased athletic excellence and cultural exchange, drawing participants and spectators from around the globe.
events.name: 2000 Summer Olympics

events.enhanced_description: On September 16, 2000, Ukrainian journalist Georgiy Gongadze was last seen alive, a date that later became a commemoration of his death. His disappearance and subsequent murder sparked widespread protests and highlighted issues of press freedom in Ukraine.
events.name: Georgiy Gongadze's Last Sighting

events.enhanced_description: On September 26, 2000, the Greek ferry Express Samina sank off the coast of Paros, resulting in the tragic loss of 80 lives among over 500 passengers. This incident is remembered as one of Greece's worst maritime disasters.
events.name: Sinking of Express Samina

events.enhanced_description: On September 28, 2000, Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount in East Jerusalem, an act that ignited tensions and sparked the Second Intifada. This visit is often cited as a catalyst for the ensuing violence and unrest.
events.name: Ariel Sharon's Visit to Temple Mount

events.enhanced_description: The killing of Muhammad al-Durrah on September 30, 2000, became a symbol of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, as the boy was shot during a gunfight between Israeli forces and Palestinians. The incident sparked international outrage and became a focal point in discussions about civilian casualties in conflict zones.
events.name: Killing of Muhammad al-Durrah

events.enhanced_description: On October 3, 2000, heavy rainfall led to severe flooding across Western Europe, particularly affecting the United Kingdom. The floods caused significant disruption and highlighted the region's vulnerability to extreme weather events.
events.name: Western Europe Floods

events.enhanced_description: On October 5, 2000, mass demonstrations in Belgrade led to the resignation of Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević. This event marked a pivotal moment in Serbian politics and the broader struggle for democracy in the region.
events.name: Mass Demonstrations in Belgrade

events.enhanced_description: On October 11, 2000, a catastrophic coal sludge spill occurred in Martin County, Kentucky, releasing 250 million US gallons of toxic waste into the environment. This disaster was considered more severe than the Exxon Valdez oil spill and raised significant concerns about coal mining practices.

events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 2000, the USS Cole was attacked in Aden, Yemen, by two Al-Qaeda suicide bombers who detonated explosives alongside the U.S. Navy destroyer. The attack resulted in the deaths of 17 crew members and injuries to at least 39 others, marking a significant escalation in terrorist activities against U.S. military forces.
events.name: USS Cole Bombing

events.enhanced_description: On October 17, 2000, a Great North Eastern Railway Intercity 225 Express Train derailed in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, resulting in the deaths of four people and numerous injuries. This tragic incident raised serious concerns about rail safety in the UK.
events.name: Hatfield Train Derailment

events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 2000, the Mainichi Shimbun newspaper exposed Japanese archaeologist Shinichi Fujimura as a fraud, revealing that many archaeological findings he claimed were authentic were fabricated. This scandal had significant implications for the field of archaeology in Japan.
events.name: Shinichi Fujimura Fraud Exposed

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 2000, Pakistani authorities announced the discovery of a mummy believed to be that of a Persian princess in Balochistan. This claim sparked international interest and controversy, with various governments asserting ownership until it was later revealed to be a forgery.
events.name: Discovery of Alleged Persian Princess Mummy

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 2000, Soyuz TM-31 was launched, carrying the first resident crew to the International Space Station (ISS). This mission marked a significant milestone in human space exploration, establishing a continuous human presence in space.

image.caption: Soyuz TM-31 lifts off from Baikonur Cosmodrome carrying the Expedition 1 crew.
image.date_qualification: Depicted date: 2000-10-31.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Launch of Soyuz TM-31

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 2000, Expedition 1 to the International Space Station began, marking the start of long-duration missions aboard the ISS. This expedition set the stage for ongoing scientific research and international collaboration in space.
events.name: Expedition 1 to the International Space Station
